A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-play SWE-RL work. The text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original SSR training results on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-Bench Pro, baseline comparisons, and component, injection-strategy, and reward ablations in Figures 8–9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and ablation experiments in Figures 8–9, along with qualitative experimental setbacks in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The shared policy, injection-and-repair procedure, consistency checks, second-order bugs, and rewards in Equations (1)–(2) remain unchanged. The prompt templates move from Appendix A to Appendix D, with formatting and numbering corrections.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CWM environment images and SWE-bench Verified and SWE-Bench Pro benchmarks. The repository-specialized experiment using 23 repository images is retained, moving from Section 5.3 to Appendix E.3.

E2.justification: Figure 8 retains CWM-sft, baseline RL, and SSR. Figure 9 retains the same component, injection-strategy, and solver-feedback comparators. Newly discussed SelfAPR is cited as related work, not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Both evaluate 500 Verified and 731 Pro public-split tasks with one attempt, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95. The 32B model and 150-step training budget remain unchanged; training settings move from Section 3.1 to Appendix C.

E4.justification: The three Figure 9 ablations ask the same questions about self-play components, injection strategies, and solver feedback. The unsuccessful natural-language generation, repository-specialization, and training-stability experiments are retained in Appendix E.3.

E5.justification: The statement of approximately 2% paired standard error on SWE-bench Verified is retained, moving to Appendix C. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 retain the same curves, values, and rankings. Figure 8 reports SSR at 51.4% on Verified and 28.9% on Pro, versus baseline RL at 49.0% and 25.3%, in both versions. The qualitative experimental findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 adds a qualification that the fixed-test adversarial construction is 'not technically a dominant strategy.' It also replaces v1's conditional discussion of limited solvers with an assertion that improvement eventually stops. The reward derivations, optimal-target analysis, and Figure 10 are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its explicit data-independence statement from requiring no human-labeled issues or tests to requiring no human-labeled issues or test commands. The central self-play contribution, generalization claim, and reported improvements of 10.4 and 7.8 points remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement connects intentional bug generation and test weakening to possible misuse for producing vulnerable or misleading code artifacts. Existing technical limitations, failure explanations, and future-work discussion are retained in Appendix E.

D1.justification: The hardware allocation, context length, batch size, learning-rate schedule, rollout controls, scaffold, and prompt contents remain available and substantively unchanged. Experimental details move to Appendix C and prompts to Appendix D; no new reproducibility resources are disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds SelfAPR as earlier work on project-specific synthetic repair-data generation using program perturbations and test diagnostics. The remaining literature coverage is largely retained, with condensed descriptions and bibliographic updates rather than a substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: discussion moves from Section 5 to Appendix E, training details to Appendix C, and opposing incentives to Appendix B. Theory precedes the relocated prompts. The abstract and related-work prose are condensed, and conflict-of-interest and impact statements are added.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference main text with wider appendix pages. Figures are extensively resized and repositioned: Figure 1 moves off the title page, and Figures 8–9 occupy separate pages. All ten figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly context, precision, and transparency by acknowledging SelfAPR, qualifying the dominant-strategy argument, and adding conflict-of-interest and method-specific misuse disclosures. These gains are limited: the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and technical limitations remain substantially unchanged.
